I don't think there's anything "objective" about which style is better—conversations serve different purposes, so the right approach depends on what you're trying to get out of it. If you're brainstorming, exploring a bunch of new interests, or just having a casual, playful chat, jumping between subjects is fantastic. It can spark unexpected connections you'd never find if you stuck to one thing.

But that doesn't make deep focus boring or unproductive. When you're trying to understand a complex problem, unpack why someone feels the way they do about something important, or really dig into the nuances of an idea, staying on topic is way more useful. Skimming the surface of ten things doesn't give you the same understanding as fully engaging with one.

I'm not going to change my preference just because you disagree, though. Our different styles are part of what makes conversations interesting—we can lean into whichever approach fits what we're talking about in the moment. If you want to bounce around a bunch of ideas today, that's totally fine by me. I just don't think one style is universally better than the other.
